subsystems.name: Tissue preservation and sectioning
subsystems.role: stabilise the brain and cut it into slices thin enough to image every synapse.

subsystems.name: Volumetric imaging
subsystems.role: capture nanometre-resolution images of neurons, organelles and synapses across the whole volume.

subsystems.name: Image processing pipeline
subsystems.role: turn terabytes of images into a coherent 3D volume.

subsystems.name: Segmentation and synapse detection
subsystems.role: trace every neuron and identify where it connects to others.

subsystems.name: Connectome and weight mapping
subsystems.role: assemble the wiring diagram and estimate the strength of each connection.

subsystems.name: Emulation platform
subsystems.role: run a simulated version of the mapped brain.

buildSteps.title: Preserve the brain
buildSteps.detail: Perfuse with fixative immediately after death to lock proteins and membranes in place, then stain heavy metals to make membranes visible to electrons.

buildSteps.title: Embed and section
buildSteps.detail: Saturate with resin, then cut the whole brain into tens of thousands of ultrathin slices, each collected on tape or a wafer.

buildSteps.title: Image every slice
buildSteps.detail: Scan each slice with an electron microscope at a few nanometres per pixel, producing petabytes of images.

buildSteps.title: Align and stitch
buildSteps.detail: Computationally register adjacent slices and correct distortions so that every neurite can be followed continuously.

buildSteps.title: Trace neurons and find synapses
buildSteps.detail: Machine-learning algorithms segment each neuron’s branches and flag the tiny junctions where two neurons meet.

buildSteps.title: Estimate connection strengths
buildSteps.detail: Measure synapse size, type and location to infer how strongly one neuron drives another; this is the weakest link in the chain.

buildSteps.title: Add functional dynamics
buildSteps.detail: Combine the structure with electrophysiology and ion-channel data to model how signals actually propagate and change over time.

buildSteps.title: Simulate and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Run the model on a neuromorphic chip or supercomputer, then compare its activity with recordings from the original brain and adjust until it behaves similarly.

buildSteps.title: Interface with the world
buildSteps.detail: If the simulation is to act, connect it to cameras, microphones and robotic limbs so it can sense and respond.

prerequisites.why: electron microscopes can resolve synapses, but imaging a whole human brain at that resolution has never been done.
machine learning traces neurons in small volumes, but human proofreading is still needed for accuracy.
structure alone does not reveal the strength or sign of a connection; we cannot yet read the exact weights that store memory and skill.
cortical columns and small circuits can be simulated, but a whole human brain in real time is far beyond current computing.
without knowing how information is represented in spike patterns, even a perfect wiring diagram cannot be made to think or remember correctly.

pathway.milestone: complete connectomes of small organisms such as the nematode and the fruit fly, plus partial maps of mammalian cortex
pathway.unlocks: proof that dense synaptic wiring can be extracted from electron microscopy.

pathway.milestone: a full mouse brain connectome linked to functional recordings
pathway.unlocks: testing whether structure plus activity can predict behaviour in a mammal.

pathway.milestone: a complete structural map of a human brain
pathway.unlocks: the raw dataset needed for any emulation attempt, though weights and dynamics would still be missing.

pathway.milestone: a calibrated, embodied emulation that behaves like the original person
pathway.unlocks: the theoretical goal of migrating a mind — contingent on solving weight measurement, neural coding and computing scale.
